content: Plant Disease Detection Using Deep Learning: A Comparative 1. Introduction Crop diseases reduce agricultural yield by nearly twenty percent every year in India. Farmers in Guntur district often identify leaf diseases late, which causes heavy losses to chilli and cotton crops. This paper compares three convolutional neural networks for automatic leaf disease classification using photographs taken in real field conditions. 2. Dataset

The dataset contains 12,000 labelled leaf images collected from farms across Andhra Pradesh. Images are divided into 70 percent training, 15 percent validation and 15 percent testing. Study A. All models were trained for fifty epochs using the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.001 and a batch size of 32.

5. Results Table 1 shows the test accuracy of the three networks. ResNet50 achieved the highest accuracy while MobileNet was the fastest model. Mildew was the hardest class because its symptoms look similar to early stage rust on young leaves.

7. Discussion Although ResNet50 gave the best accuracy, MobileNet is more suitable for smartphones because it needs only 14 MB of memory. Farmers can therefore run the model offline in the field without an internet connection. MobileNet processed about 45 images per second on a mid-range phone. 8. Conclusion

This study showed that deep learning can detect leaf diseases with accuracy above ninety percent. Future work will extend the dataset to include pest damage and nutrient deficiency symptoms.
